moments.title: Tempo (BPM)
moments.text: 80 BPM: relaxed, unhurried. Count along: 1, 2, 3, 4.
moments.why: Set it by your cutting pace. Quick cuts sit well between 120 and 150; slow beauty shots between 70 and 100.

clips.title: Tempo (BPM): 80 BPM
clips.body: Beats per minute is the strongest energy knob you have. The same groove at 80 feels relaxed, at 120 it walks with purpose, at 160 it runs. Pick tempo from the pace of your edit: fast cuts want 120 to 150, slow product beauty shots want 70 to 100.

moments.title: Tempo (BPM)
moments.text: 120 BPM: the same groove walking with purpose.
moments.why: Set it by your cutting pace. Quick cuts sit well between 120 and 150; slow beauty shots between 70 and 100.

moments.title: Bar
moments.text: Bar 2. Four beats make a bar; at 120 BPM a bar is exactly 2 seconds.
moments.why: At 120 BPM a bar lasts exactly two seconds. Place every reveal on a bar line.

moments.title: Downbeat
moments.text: Beat 1 of bar 3: a downbeat. Cuts and reveals feel right here.
moments.why: Cut the reveal, the title and the end card on a downbeat and the edit feels inevitable.

clips.title: Tempo (BPM): 120 BPM
clips.body: Beats per minute is the strongest energy knob you have. The same groove at 80 feels relaxed, at 120 it walks with purpose, at 160 it runs. Pick tempo from the pace of your edit: fast cuts want 120 to 150, slow product beauty shots want 70 to 100.

moments.title: Tempo (BPM)
moments.text: 160 BPM: the same groove running. Everything feels urgent.
moments.why: Set it by your cutting pace. Quick cuts sit well between 120 and 150; slow beauty shots between 70 and 100.

clips.title: Tempo (BPM): 160 BPM
clips.body: Beats per minute is the strongest energy knob you have. The same groove at 80 feels relaxed, at 120 it walks with purpose, at 160 it runs. Pick tempo from the pace of your edit: fast cuts want 120 to 150, slow product beauty shots want 70 to 100.

moments.title: Four-on-the-floor
moments.text: Kick on every beat. Watch the low row: four even hits per bar.
moments.why: Momentum without apology. The engine under house, disco and most launch montages.

moments.title: Backbeat
moments.text: Now the kick plays 1 and 3, the snare answers on 2 and 4.
moments.why: The head-nod of pop and hip hop. Familiar, steady and easy to cut to.

moments.title: Half-time
moments.text: Snare only on beat 3. Same tempo, but it suddenly feels slow and heavy.
moments.why: Makes a drop feel heavier without changing the tempo your edit is cut to.

clips.title: Three drum feels
clips.body: Four-on-the-floor (kick on every beat) pushes forward like a dance floor. The backbeat (snare on 2 and 4) is the pop head-nod. Half-time puts the snare on beat 3 only, so the same tempo suddenly feels twice as slow and heavy. That trick makes a drop feel huge without changing the BPM your edit is cut to.

moments.title: Hi-hats
moments.text: Straight 16th hats: every tick exactly on the grid.
moments.why: The cheapest way to raise energy: double them, from eighths to sixteenths.

moments.title: Swing
moments.text: Swing: every second tick is pushed late. Look at the uneven gaps in the top row.
moments.why: Swing reads as human and unhurried. Straight time reads as engineered.

clips.title: Straight vs swing
clips.body: Straight 16th notes sit exactly on the grid and sound engineered, which suits precise tech. Swing delays every second note a little, and the rhythm starts to lope. That reads as human, relaxed and crafted: lo-fi, UK garage, boom bap.

moments.title: Chords / pad
moments.text: Chords on the beats. Stiff, like a metronome.
moments.why: Slow chord changes feel calm and expensive. Fast ones feel busy.

moments.title: Syncopation
moments.text: Same chords, now between the beats. It starts to bounce.
moments.why: Brings bounce and life. Keep it gentle under a narrator.

clips.title: Syncopation
clips.body: Hits that land between the beats make music feel funky and alive. The same chords on the beat sound stiff and corporate. Use it for energy, but keep it gentle under a narrator.

moments.title: Major vs minor
moments.text: C major: bright and resolved.
moments.why: Minor at a groove tempo reads as cool and premium, not sad.

moments.title: Major vs minor
moments.text: C minor: one note in each chord drops. Darker, more serious.
moments.why: Minor at a groove tempo reads as cool and premium, not sad.

clips.title: Major vs minor
clips.body: Same melody, only the scale changes. Major is bright and resolved. Minor is darker and more serious, and at a decent tempo it reads as cool and premium rather than sad. Most house, synthwave and trailer music is minor for that reason.

moments.title: Lydian
moments.text: Lydian: listen for the raised 4th (F#). It floats.
moments.why: Wonder and optimism, the future looking bright. Made for capability reveals.

moments.title: Dorian
moments.text: Dorian: minor, but the 6th is raised. Cool and hopeful.
moments.why: Smart and cool. The colour of deep house, lo-fi and funk.

moments.title: Phrygian
moments.text: Phrygian: the 2nd drops a half step (Db). Instantly tense.
moments.why: Security, intrusion, threat. Use it when the film should feel dangerous.

moments.title: Mixolydian
moments.text: Mixolydian: major with a flat 7th (Bb). Swagger.
moments.why: Confidence with a swagger. Fun without the cheese.

clips.title: Modes: four moods from one root
clips.body: A mode is a scale with one "flavour note". Lydian floats (wonder, optimism, the future is bright). Dorian is minor with a hopeful lift (smart, cool). Phrygian is dark and tense (security, hacker, threat). Mixolydian is major with swagger (confident, fun without cheese).

moments.title: Chords / pad
moments.text: A plain C triad: three notes. Simple.
moments.why: Slow chord changes feel calm and expensive. Fast ones feel busy.

moments.title: 7th and 9th chords
moments.text: Add a 7th: Cmaj7. Dreamy, sophisticated.
moments.why: Sevenths sound dreamy; ninths sound lush and expensive.

moments.title: 7th and 9th chords
moments.text: Add a 9th: Cmaj9. Lush and expensive.
moments.why: Sevenths sound dreamy; ninths sound lush and expensive.

moments.title: Suspended chord
moments.text: Csus4 hangs like a question...
moments.why: Leave it hanging through the build, resolve it on the end card, and it lands like an answer.

moments.title: Suspended chord
moments.text: ...and resolves to C. The answer. Perfect under an end card.
moments.why: Leave it hanging through the build, resolve it on the end card, and it lands like an answer.

clips.title: Chord colour
clips.body: Adding notes changes the colour of a chord. A plain triad is simple; a major 7th turns dreamy; a 9th sounds lush and expensive. A sus chord leaves a question hanging, and resolving it lands the answer, which makes a fine move for an end card.

moments.title: Chord progression
moments.text: C G Am F: the pop anthem. Uplifting, but everywhere.
moments.why: Where the loop starts and ends shapes the feeling more than the chords themselves.

moments.title: Chord progression
moments.text: Am F C G: the same chords starting from minor. Bittersweet, cinematic.
moments.why: Where the loop starts and ends shapes the feeling more than the chords themselves.

moments.title: Button
moments.text: Ending on C, the home chord, sounds finished.
moments.why: Land it on the end card and let it ring. Always stronger than a fade-out.

clips.title: Same chords, different home
clips.body: C G Am F is the pop anthem and risks sounding generic. Start the same four chords on Am and they turn bittersweet and cinematic, the EDM and trailer staple. Where a progression starts and ends changes the feeling more than which chords it uses.

moments.title: Waveform
moments.text: Sine: pure and soft. The sound of sub-bass.
moments.why: Sine is soft and pure. Sawtooth is bright and buzzing.

moments.title: Waveform
moments.text: Triangle: gentle, flute-like.
moments.why: Sine is soft and pure. Sawtooth is bright and buzzing.

moments.title: Waveform
moments.text: Square: hollow and retro, the 8-bit sound.
moments.why: Sine is soft and pure. Sawtooth is bright and buzzing.

moments.title: Waveform
moments.text: Sawtooth: bright and buzzy. Most synth sounds start here.
moments.why: Sine is soft and pure. Sawtooth is bright and buzzing.

clips.title: The four raw waveforms
clips.body: Every synth sound starts from a few shapes. Sine is pure and soft (sub-bass, clean tones). Triangle is gentle. Square is hollow and retro. Sawtooth is bright and buzzy and is the raw material for most pads, leads and basses.

moments.title: Filter sweep
moments.text: The filter is almost closed: muffled, far away.
moments.why: The most natural way to build towards a reveal.

moments.title: Build
moments.text: It keeps opening. You can see the spectrum growing to the right.
moments.why: The musical shape of the tension before a reveal.

moments.title: Filter sweep
moments.text: Snap shut: back to the muffled sound.
moments.why: The most natural way to build towards a reveal.

clips.title: Filter sweep
clips.body: A low-pass filter removes the highs. Closed, the sound is muffled and far away; opening it over a few bars is the most natural way to build towards a reveal. Snapping it shut zooms back out.

moments.title: Pluck
moments.text: Plucks: instant start, quick fade. Notice the short blocks.
moments.why: Crisp and precise, and it leaves space for a voice.

moments.title: Pad
moments.text: Pads: slow swell, long tail. The blocks stretch across the bar.
moments.why: The emotional glue behind everything else.

clips.title: Pluck vs pad
clips.body: An envelope shapes how a note starts and fades. Plucks hit instantly and die fast: crisp, precise, and they leave gaps for a voice. Pads swell in slowly and hang: emotional, but they fill the space.

moments.title: Reverb
moments.text: Bone dry: close and modern.
moments.why: A large, dark reverb sounds expensive. Dry sounds close and modern.

moments.title: Reverb
moments.text: Big reverb: the notes sit in a large room.
moments.why: A large, dark reverb sounds expensive. Dry sounds close and modern.

moments.title: Delay / echo
moments.text: Delay: each note echoes in rhythm.
moments.why: Adds depth and motion without adding a single part.

clips.title: Reverb and delay
clips.body: Dry sounds close and modern. A big reverb sounds expensive and cinematic, while a bright wash of it on everything sounds amateur. Delay repeats the notes in rhythm and adds depth and motion.

moments.title: Chords / pad
moments.text: Kick and pad simply play together.
moments.why: Slow chord changes feel calm and expensive. Fast ones feel busy.

moments.title: Sidechain pumping
moments.text: Now the pad ducks on every kick. Watch the chord lane pulse.
moments.why: The euphoric push of house, French touch and future bass.

clips.title: Sidechain pumping
clips.body: The pad ducks every time the kick hits, so the track breathes. That pulse is the sound of house, French touch and future bass drops.

moments.title: Intro / hook
moments.text: Hook from the first frame: a pulse and a pad. Energy 3 of 10.
moments.why: On a social feed the most distinctive sound must arrive in the first second.

moments.title: Build
moments.text: Hats join and the filter opens: we are building.
moments.why: The musical shape of the tension before a reveal.

moments.title: Riser
moments.text: A white-noise riser starts climbing towards bar 5.
moments.why: Builds anticipation, and must end exactly on the downbeat of the reveal.

moments.title: Kick
moments.text: Drums come in. Watch the bottom row of the drum lane: that is the kick.
moments.why: The moment the kick enters is usually the moment the picture starts to move.

moments.title: Stop-down
moments.text: One beat of silence. The intake of breath.
moments.why: The reveal lands because of the silence before it, not because it is loud.

moments.title: Drop
moments.text: DROP: full drums and bass on the downbeat. Your product reveal goes here.
moments.why: Put the product reveal exactly here.

moments.title: Bass
moments.text: The bass enters: everything suddenly has weight.
moments.why: Phone speakers barely reach it, so good bass carries a few upper harmonics too.

moments.title: Button
moments.text: The button: one final chord on the end card, left to ring.
moments.why: Land it on the end card and let it ring. Always stronger than a fade-out.

clips.title: Build, silence, drop, button
clips.body: This is the whole shape of a launch video in 15 seconds at 128 BPM. A hook from the first frame, a build with a riser, one beat of silence, then the drop exactly on the reveal. It ends with a button hit on the end card. The drop lands because of the silence before it, not because it is loud.

moments.title: The voice band
moments.text: A voice-over bed: pad low, ticks very high. The middle stays empty for a voice.
moments.why: Keep the music quiet here whenever someone is talking.

moments.title: Melody / hook
moments.text: A bright lead enters right in the voice band. A narrator would fight it.
moments.why: Keep it clear of the voice-over and let it answer in the pauses.

clips.title: Music under a voice
clips.body: A voice lives in the middle frequencies. A good bed stays low (pads, sub) and high (soft ticks) and leaves the middle empty. In bars 5 to 8 a bright lead joins in, and it would fight any narrator. Keep melodies for the gaps between sentences.

moments.title: Bass
moments.text: Pure sine sub: huge on headphones, nearly invisible on a phone.
moments.why: Phone speakers barely reach it, so good bass carries a few upper harmonics too.

moments.title: Distortion / bitcrush
moments.text: Saturation plus an octave layer: harmonics you can hear on any speaker.
moments.why: A little is warmth; a lot is attitude. It also helps bass cut through a phone.

clips.title: Bass on a phone
clips.body: Phone speakers can barely play anything below about 150 Hz. A pure sine sub disappears on them. Add saturation and an octave-up layer and the harmonics let the ear hear the bass anyway. Play this one on your phone.

clips.title: Tech keynote minimal
clips.use: Feature walkthroughs, interface animation, SaaS launches, hardware beauty shots
clips.prompt: Instrumental minimal tech-keynote cue, 112 BPM, F Lydian. Plucked synth arpeggio alternating F major and G major, tiny high-frequency ticks on 16th notes, rim clicks on 2 and 4, soft kick on 1 and 3, round sub bass, dark airy pad. Clean, precise, optimistic. No vocals, no crash cymbals. Ends on a single piano chord.
clips.note: Glass, aluminium and a raised fourth. The sound of a product that simply works.

clips.prompt: Instrumental electronic launch cue, 120 BPM, A minor. One repeated synth note in 16ths with a slowly opening and closing low-pass filter, soft four-on-the-floor kick, sustained sub bass, airy minor-9th pad, quiet offbeat hats. Confident and engineered. No vocals. One-beat stop before the drop; ends on a button chord.
clips.note: One note, sixteen times a bar, and a filter that breathes. Engineered confidence.

clips.prompt: Instrumental future bass, 150 BPM half-time, F major (Bbmaj7 C6 Am7 Dm7). Build with snare roll and white-noise riser, then a drop of rhythmically chopped supersaw chords pumping against the kick, clap on beat 3, trap hi-hat rolls, vowel-filtered pluck hook. Euphoric. No vocals.
clips.note: A held breath, one beat of silence, then every speaker at once.

clips.title: Corporate uplifting
clips.use: Nowhere near a technology audience. It signals stock music at once
clips.prompt: (What to avoid) Stock "uplifting corporate": ukulele-like plucks, claps on 2 and 4, glockenspiel melody, C G Am F. If you see these words in a prompt, expect generic stock music.
clips.note: Claps, glockenspiel and C G Am F. Learn it by heart, then never ask for it.

bpm.title: Tempo (BPM)
bpm.def: Tempo, counted in beats per minute. The strongest lever on energy you have: 70 breathes, 120 strides, 160 runs.
bpm.why: Set it by your cutting pace. Quick cuts sit well between 120 and 150; slow beauty shots between 70 and 100.

bar.title: Bar
bar.def: Four beats, counted as one unit. Musicians and editors plan in bars, not seconds.
bar.why: At 120 BPM a bar lasts exactly two seconds. Place every reveal on a bar line.

downbeat.title: Downbeat
downbeat.def: The first beat of a bar, and the heaviest.
downbeat.why: Cut the reveal, the title and the end card on a downbeat and the edit feels inevitable.

four-on-the-floor.title: Four-on-the-floor
four-on-the-floor.def: A kick drum on every beat: one, two, three, four.
four-on-the-floor.why: Momentum without apology. The engine under house, disco and most launch montages.

backbeat.title: Backbeat
backbeat.def: Kick on one and three, snare or clap on two and four.
backbeat.why: The head-nod of pop and hip hop. Familiar, steady and easy to cut to.

half-time.title: Half-time
half-time.def: The snare moves to beat three alone, so the groove feels half as fast.
half-time.why: Makes a drop feel heavier without changing the tempo your edit is cut to.

two-step.title: 2-step
two-step.def: A broken kick, on one and the 'and' of three, in place of a kick on every beat.
two-step.why: It skips where house marches. The lilt of UK garage and drum and bass.

hi-hats.title: Hi-hats
hi-hats.def: The ticking cymbals that fill the gaps between the drums.
hi-hats.why: The cheapest way to raise energy: double them, from eighths to sixteenths.

swing.title: Swing
swing.def: Every second small note arrives a fraction late, and the rhythm begins to lope.
swing.why: Swing reads as human and unhurried. Straight time reads as engineered.

syncopation.title: Syncopation
syncopation.def: Accents placed between the beats rather than on them.
syncopation.why: Brings bounce and life. Keep it gentle under a narrator.

kick.title: Kick
kick.def: The low drum that marks the pulse.
kick.why: The moment the kick enters is usually the moment the picture starts to move.

bass.title: Bass
bass.def: The lowest line in the music. It carries the weight and names the chord.
bass.why: Phone speakers barely reach it, so good bass carries a few upper harmonics too.

chords.title: Chords / pad
chords.def: Several notes sounded together: the harmony that sets the mood.
chords.why: Slow chord changes feel calm and expensive. Fast ones feel busy.

melody.title: Melody / hook
melody.def: The line you could hum. The identity of the piece.
melody.why: Keep it clear of the voice-over and let it answer in the pauses.

arpeggio.title: Arpeggio
arpeggio.def: A chord played one note at a time, in a pattern.
arpeggio.why: Reads as motion and computation, things quietly happening. A technology favourite.

ostinato.title: Ostinato / pulse
ostinato.def: A short figure repeated, bar after bar.
ostinato.why: Drives a montage without competing with the voice over it.

major-minor.title: Major vs minor
major-minor.def: Major sounds bright and settled; minor sounds darker and more serious.
major-minor.why: Minor at a groove tempo reads as cool and premium, not sad.

lydian.title: Lydian
lydian.def: A major scale with its fourth note raised. It floats.
lydian.why: Wonder and optimism, the future looking bright. Made for capability reveals.
hear: Modes: four moods from one root

dorian.title: Dorian
dorian.def: A minor scale with its sixth note raised. Minor, with a lift of hope.
dorian.why: Smart and cool. The colour of deep house, lo-fi and funk.
hear: Modes: four moods from one root

phrygian.title: Phrygian
phrygian.def: A minor scale with its second note lowered. Tense, faintly menacing.
phrygian.why: Security, intrusion, threat. Use it when the film should feel dangerous.
hear: Modes: four moods from one root

mixolydian.title: Mixolydian
mixolydian.def: A major scale with its seventh note lowered.
mixolydian.why: Confidence with a swagger. Fun without the cheese.
hear: Modes: four moods from one root

sus.title: Suspended chord
sus.def: A chord with its third replaced, so it hangs unresolved.
sus.why: Leave it hanging through the build, resolve it on the end card, and it lands like an answer.

seventh.title: 7th and 9th chords
seventh.def: Extra notes stacked on a chord for colour.
seventh.why: Sevenths sound dreamy; ninths sound lush and expensive.

progression.title: Chord progression
progression.def: The order in which chords arrive, usually a loop of two to four.
progression.why: Where the loop starts and ends shapes the feeling more than the chords themselves.

filter-sweep.title: Filter sweep
filter-sweep.def: A filter opening slowly, letting the bright frequencies back in.
filter-sweep.why: The most natural way to build towards a reveal.

riser.title: Riser
riser.def: A sound climbing in pitch, brightness or volume.
riser.why: Builds anticipation, and must end exactly on the downbeat of the reveal.

stop-down.title: Stop-down
stop-down.def: A deliberate silence, usually one beat, just before an impact.
stop-down.why: The reveal lands because of the silence before it, not because it is loud.

drop.title: Drop
drop.def: The moment the full arrangement arrives after a build.
drop.why: Put the product reveal exactly here.

impact.title: Impact / hit
impact.def: A kick, a crash and a low boom struck together.
impact.why: Punctuation for a cut, a title or a reveal.

button.title: Button
button.def: One decisive final chord or hit.
button.why: Land it on the end card and let it ring. Always stronger than a fade-out.

breakdown.title: Breakdown
breakdown.def: A passage where the drums step out and the harmony stays.
breakdown.why: Room for the most important line of your voice-over.

sidechain.title: Sidechain pumping
sidechain.def: Everything else ducks each time the kick lands, so the track breathes.
sidechain.why: The euphoric push of house, French touch and future bass.

reverb.title: Reverb
reverb.def: The sound of a room around the notes.
reverb.why: A large, dark reverb sounds expensive. Dry sounds close and modern.

delay.title: Delay / echo
delay.def: Notes repeated in rhythm, each echo softer than the last.
delay.why: Adds depth and motion without adding a single part.

pluck.title: Pluck
pluck.def: A note that starts instantly and dies quickly.
pluck.why: Crisp and precise, and it leaves space for a voice.

pad.title: Pad
pad.def: A sustained tone that swells in slowly and hangs.
pad.why: The emotional glue behind everything else.

supersaw.title: Supersaw
supersaw.def: Many slightly detuned sawtooth waves stacked into one.
supersaw.why: Huge, wide and euphoric. The sound of a festival drop.

808.def: A long, booming electronic kick, tuned so it doubles as the bass.
808.why: The low end of trap and phonk.

distortion.title: Distortion / bitcrush
distortion.def: Sound roughened on purpose, from gentle warmth to broken grit.
distortion.why: A little is warmth; a lot is attitude. It also helps bass cut through a phone.

drone.title: Drone / pedal
drone.def: One low note held beneath everything.
drone.why: Tension in trailers and countdowns, or deep calm in ambient.

motif.title: Motif
motif.def: A two-to-five note idea that keeps returning.
motif.why: Bring it back on the end card and it becomes your sonic signature.

build.title: Build
build.def: A stretch where layers, brightness and density rise together.
build.why: The musical shape of the tension before a reveal.

intro.title: Intro / hook
intro.def: The opening seconds, which set the tone for everything after.
intro.why: On a social feed the most distinctive sound must arrive in the first second.

waveform.title: Waveform
waveform.def: The raw shape of a synthesised sound: sine, triangle, square or sawtooth.
waveform.why: Sine is soft and pure. Sawtooth is bright and buzzing.

voice-band.title: The voice band
voice-band.def: The frequencies speech lives in, roughly 300 Hz to 3 kHz.
voice-band.why: Keep the music quiet here whenever someone is talking.

texture.title: Texture
texture.def: Noise, crackle or air beneath the music.
texture.why: Gives a sense of place: vinyl, rain, a room.
